anomaly_signals.detail: 622 errors out of 1000 spans (62.2% error rate) — acting as the primary blast radius amplifier for the cascading failure.
255 errors out of 1000 spans (25.5% error rate), likely propagating failures from postgres-auth (134/1000, 13.4% error rate).
225 errors out of 494 spans (45.5% error rate) — nearly half of all agent invocations are failing, consistent with agentic cascading failure.
220 errors out of 487 spans (45.2% error rate) corroborated by 226 genai_tool_failures — tool execution is critically degraded, stalling agent workflows.
136 errors out of 410 spans (33.2% error rate), mirrored by postgres-payments at 104/410 (25.4%) — payment flow is significantly impaired.
128 errors out of 872 spans (14.7% error rate) contributing to p99 latency of ~29.4s system-wide; likely experiencing timeout/overload due to upstream agent retry storms.
32 genai token truncations detected — context windows being exceeded, possibly due to bloated prompts from agent retry loops or accumulated memory context.
93 errors out of 494 spans (18.8% error rate) — memory retrieval failures likely degrading agent context quality and exacerbating tool failures.
61 errors out of 247 spans (24.7% error rate) — orchestration layer is propagating failures across the agentic pipeline.

recommended_action: Immediately throttle agent-service retry policies and circuit-break tool-executor to halt the cascading amplification. Investigate postgres-auth and postgres-payments for root DB degradation. Rate-limit LLM requests to Gemini to reduce token truncations and timeout pressure. Review memory-service context payloads to prevent prompt bloat.
summary: A confirmed agentic cascading failure is in progress: 25.7% of all spans are in ERROR state with a p99 latency of ~29.4 seconds. The failure originates from degraded database and tool-executor layers, propagating through agent-service, auth-service, and payments-service, ultimately saturating the api-gateway with a 62% error rate and generating 226 tool failures and 32 LLM token truncations.
